subject: genetics
question: **Type:** concept Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences. An enzyme that cuts the two strands at staggered positions leaves short single-stranded overhangs at each end. What are these ends called?
explanation: A staggered cut leaves single-stranded overhangs that can base-pair with complementary overhangs from another DNA molecule, which is why they are called sticky ends and why DNA from different sources is so easy to join. A blunt end results when an enzyme cuts both strands straight across at the same position, the error behind A. C mistakes the palindrome property of the recognition sequence for the structure of the cut. D confuses the methylation that protects host DNA from its own restriction enzymes with the cut ends.
